findings.summary: Header-band art is still a small sticker on both new products. On desktop it is a two-to-three-piece cluster about 230–310px wide, roughly a fifth of the band, with a wide empty stretch of colour between the text and the art. It almost never pictures the page's subject. The sign-up band copies the spec's one sample nearly piece for piece: a violet hexagon, an overlapping orange pill, a large yellow star and a small pink sparkle. The pricing and docs inner-page clusters reuse its layout with a disc as the lead shape. The reference's hero (02) is a layered scene about as wide as the headline block that balances it. This gap was named in rc.3 reviews 1 and 2 and is unchanged on products the system was never tuned on. The landing front page shows what is possible: its hero is a product vignette with overlapping cards and confetti, and it reaches the reference's bar.
findings.promptFix: Size desktop header-band art by width. The art box takes about 40–45% of the band, and its SVG is `width: 100%; height: auto` in a wide viewBox of about 400×240. Build it from 4–5 pieces spread across the box: a lead shape that pictures the screen's subject in one noun (for example a key or an open door for an account screen, a group of discs for a people page, a coin stack for prices), a second-hue shape cutting into it, a 48–64px four-point star, a small sparkle and optionally a cloud. On a product's front page, prefer a vignette of the product's own UI (overlapping white cards on the band) with confetti around it. Give three sample clusters with different silhouettes, label them as structure only, and say that reusing a sample's shapes or arrangement counts as a copy. Art narrower than a third of the band, or a disc and pill that picture nothing, is a sticker, not a scene.
findings.specRule: .ms-field__art > svg { height: 100%; min-height: var(--size-art); max-width: 100%; } … <!-- Header-band cluster, one of many: lead hexagon, overlapping pill, large star + small sparkle --> <svg viewBox="0 0 240 200">

findings.summary: The pricing plan cards are white boxes with 2px grey borders (lilac at night) and mid-size prices, set beside one violet selected plan, so the page reads as a stock SaaS pricing grid. The reference never borders a card. It carries figures on borderless tone-on-tone fields where one big bold number dominates (08). The spec writes the border into the plan card, against its own no-border card rule. This has been open since rc.1 and now shows on a new product.
findings.promptFix: Option cards (plans, tiers, packages) follow the card rule: no border and no shadow, `radius.lg`. Unselected options are `color.surface.subtle` (cream by day, indigo at night). The selected option is the one saturated field, with on-field text and the check disc. The plan name is an eyebrow, and the price is the card's largest type, `font.size.h2`, bold and tight. Depth comes from tone alone.
findings.specRule: Plan card: white, `radius.md`, 2px `color.border.default`; selected: `color.field.violet`, white text and check disc.

findings.summary: In the dark appearance the pricing night band turns purple, and the selected plan is violet on top of it, so the plan the page is selling barely separates from its ground. The bordered indigo plans beside it make the first screen muddy. In the reference's night palette (03), a deep navy ground lets one bright panel, knob or pill carry the eye.
findings.promptFix: Keep `color.field.night` a deep navy in both appearances, a step off the dark page, and never purple. A highlighted item on any field must come from a clearly different hue from that field in both appearances (yellow, blue, or white with ink text on a dark band). Never set a saturated panel on a field of a neighbouring hue.

findings.summary: The no-results search state uses three yellow dots as its only art. That is the system's loading glyph, so 'nothing found' reads as 'still loading'. The state also offers no next step. The reference states outcomes with a pictogram of the subject (07).

In dark mode every page on both products ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer. It is the one light element at night. The spec puts the bar on `surface.inverse`, which is white in the dark table. The reference's night band (03) stays dark to the edge. Named in rc.3 review 2 and still open.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and at night a step darker than the navy page, with white text. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | … `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: The landing front page's stat row is three short, wide strips with figures of about 24px, so no number dominates. The reference's colour tiles (08) are tall saturated fields, each carried by one big bold number under a small eyebrow. The spec sets the stat number at h3.

Small glyphs are often chosen without meaning or drawn too small for their plate. The docs page-foot controls (feedback, previous/next) carry a ring, a zigzag and bubbles unrelated to their labels, and they repeat on every page in a new hue. The pictograms on the customer-category covers fill only about a quarter of each cover, so the covers read as empty colour blocks. The sign-up success screen pairs an envelope with an unrelated floating moon. The reference chooses each glyph for its row and fills its plates (05, 07).

On phones, hero bands run long. The docs front page stacks its art as its own row under the pills, so the yellow band fills the whole first screen. Sign-up and customers leave about 150px of white below the arc before the content. The reference phone (04) keeps the band compact and tucks the art at the edge.

Keyboard focus on text links (the wordmark, top-bar links) is a flush, square-cornered box that looks like the browser default. Pills get the reference's rounded ring offset by 2px (11). Open since rc.2.

Reveal-on-view content never appears in some full-page captures. On the landing front page the features grid is left blank, the testimonials row is empty in dark, and one card of the hero vignette sits near zero opacity. This comes from the agent's observer and timing; the spec says content must be complete without the runtime class.

On phones the docs breadcrumb is squeezed beside the band's corner cluster and wraps, leaving a separator and the current page alone on a second line. In the changelog, change-type tags size to their labels, so the entry text after them starts at a different indent on each line.

notes: Review: 78/78 checklist items by 4 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/morning-shapes/0.1.0-rc.3/review-3-holdout).

On both new products the language carries clearly. Yolk bands with sagging arcs, 64px tight headlines, blue and white pills on their ledges, ink pills with the white dot, cream panels, confetti headings and a convincing navy night palette make the two apps read as one family. The landing hero vignette is as good as the reference's 01/02.

The system's most recognisable moment, the header-band scene, falls back on inner pages to a small two-to-three-piece sticker. It is often copied from the spec's one sample and rarely pictures its page, so the signature misses the bar.

Pricing is the weakest screen. Its bordered stock-SaaS plan cards come straight from the spec, and the purple night band muddies the selected plan. Together with the white footer bar at night, these spec-caused gaps are what keep the result below the reference's craft.
